post.caption: An emerald named for lions. In October 2018, miners at the Kagem mine in Zambia found a rough emerald of 5,655 carats, almost 2.5 pounds. Inkalamu means lion in Bemba, a Zambian language, and the name honors two groups that protect carnivores. Gemfields said it would share 10 percent of the sale with them. The emerald before it, Insofu, was named for an elephant. Inkalamu sold at an auction in Singapore in November 2018 to the Indian jeweler Diacolor, and in June 2019 it went on show behind glass in Delhi.
